dossier.purpose: MCP server (TypeScript on Node) that exposes Firecrawl web operations as six MCP tools - firecrawl_scrape (one URL -> markdown/html/json/screenshot etc., optional onlyMainContent), firecrawl_map, firecrawl_search, firecrawl_crawl, firecrawl_check_crawl_status, firecrawl_extract - by wrapping the @mendable/firecrawl-js client (src/index.ts:234-565). Facts bearing on the stated needs: (1) fetching a chosen URL exists only as the MCP tool firecrawl_scrape; the package ships no shell CLI for it (the firecrawl-mcp bin only starts the server, package.json:6-8) and the tool returns the SDK response as JSON text (src/index.ts:156-158, 268-269), so metadata fields come from the Firecrawl API rather than from this repo; (2) page interaction exists only as the `actions` array on firecrawl_scrape (and inside scrapeOptions of search/crawl): wait, screenshot, scroll, scrape, click, write, press, executeJavascript, generatePDF (src/index.ts:164-166, 205-220). It is absent when CLOUD_SERVICE=true, is not mentioned in the README, is sent in a single client.scrape call (src/index.ts:268), has no tab, navigation or session-persistence action types, and has no shell-callable form. A Firecrawl API key (cloud) or a self-hosted Firecrawl API URL is required (README.md:182-190).

claims.claim: 'A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation that integrates with Firecrawl for web scraping capabilities.'
Features: web scraping, crawling and discovery; search and content extraction; deep research and batch scraping; automatic retries and rate limiting; cloud and self-hosted support; SSE support.
Run with env FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY npx -y firecrawl-mcp; stdio is the default transport and SSE is opt-in with SSE_LOCAL=true at http://localhost:3000/sse.
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY is 'Required when using cloud API (default)' and optional for a self-hosted instance reached through FIRECRAWL_API_URL; keys come from a firecrawl.dev account.

firecrawl_scrape: 'Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options', best when you know exactly which page has the information; returns 'Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified'; example options: formats, onlyMainContent, waitFor, timeout, mobile, includeTags, excludeTags, skipTlsVerification.
For many known URLs use firecrawl_batch_scrape ('built-in rate limiting and parallel processing') and poll with firecrawl_check_batch_status.
firecrawl_crawl starts an asynchronous crawl; 'Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages'.
firecrawl_map discovers URLs on a site; firecrawl_search searches the web and can optionally scrape the results.
firecrawl_extract: 'Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.'

Retries: FIRECRAWL_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS / INITIAL_DELAY / MAX_DELAY / BACKOFF_FACTOR (defaults 3, 1000, 10000, 2); 'Automatically retries failed requests due to rate limits' with exponential backoff; rate limiting is attributed to 'Firecrawl's built-in' capabilities.
Credit monitoring: FIRECRAWL_CREDIT_WARNING_THRESHOLD (1000) and FIRECRAWL_CREDIT_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD (100); 'Tracks API credit consumption for cloud API usage'.
'The server includes comprehensive logging': operation status and progress, performance metrics, credit usage monitoring, rate limit tracking, error conditions.
Client setup examples for Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code and Claude Desktop, all launching npx -y firecrawl-mcp with FIRECRAWL_API_KEY in env.
Development flow is npm install, npm run build, npm test; license stated as 'MIT License - see LICENSE file for details'.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics, crash-reporting or update-check code in this repo (grep of README, source, configs and workflows found none; the only hit is the 'changeTracking' format name, src/index.ts:183). Network use: every tool call goes through @mendable/firecrawl-js (src/index.ts:5, 268, 309, 394, 462, 492, 562) to the Firecrawl API - Firecrawl cloud by default, which needs a Firecrawl account and API key (README.md:82, 184-190) - or to a self-hosted Firecrawl at FIRECRAWL_API_URL (src/index.ts:119-132; README.md:187-190). The repo holds no base-URL constant, so the default cloud endpoint is defined inside the SDK (not in this checkout). Every call except check_crawl_status adds origin: 'mcp-fastmcp' (src/index.ts:134, 268, 309, 396, 464, 560). Target URLs, search queries, options, extraction prompts and any text typed by write actions are therefore sent to the Firecrawl service. dotenv loads a .env file from the working directory (src/index.ts:8). Logging is silent in stdio mode and goes to the console only in the HTTP modes (src/index.ts:54-86). HTTP modes listen on PORT (default 3000) and serve MCP plus /health (src/index.ts:110-116, 566-586).

entry_points.what: bin 'firecrawl-mcp' -> dist/index.js, compiled from src/index.ts (shebang at src/index.ts:1; tsconfig.json:6-7); starts the MCP server, stdio by default.
Server main: picks stdio, or stateless httpStream on PORT (default 3000) and HOST (default localhost; 0.0.0.0 when CLOUD_SERVICE=true), then awaits server.start().
The six MCP tool registrations (scrape, map, search, crawl, check_crawl_status, extract), each wrapping one @mendable/firecrawl-js call.
npm start -> node dist/index.js; npm run start:cloud -> CLOUD_SERVICE=true node dist/index.js (header-authenticated HTTP mode with Safe Mode).
Smithery-generated image (Dockerfile:1): ENTRYPOINT node dist/index.js on node:22-slim; no workflow builds this file.

Service image: CMD /entrypoint.sh (docker/entrypoint.sh:1-11) runs node dist/index.js in the background and nginx in the foreground on :8080 (docker/nginx.conf); no transport env var is set in the image, so CLOUD_SERVICE / SSE_LOCAL / HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER must be supplied at run time (src/index.ts:574-586).
Smithery stdio start command: node dist/index.js with FIRECRAWL_API_KEY / FIRECRAWL_API_URL taken from the Smithery config.

code.architecture: Single-file server. src/index.ts (about 595 lines) builds a FastMCP server from the forked firecrawl-fastmcp package (src/index.ts:3, 88-117), defines zod parameter schemas, and registers six tools that each call one @mendable/firecrawl-js method: scrape -> client.scrape (:268), map -> client.map (:309), search -> client.search (:394), crawl -> client.crawl (:462), check_crawl_status -> client.getCrawlStatus (:492), extract -> client.extract (:562); results are returned as JSON.stringify(response, null, 2) (:156-158). The scrape schema covers formats (markdown, html, rawHtml, screenshot, links, summary, changeTracking, json with prompt/schema), onlyMainContent, includeTags/excludeTags, waitFor, mobile, skipTlsVerification, location, storeInCache, maxAge and `actions` (:171-232). The per-session API key comes from `authenticate` (:93-109): from Authorization Bearer / x-firecrawl-api-key / x-api-key headers when CLOUD_SERVICE=true (:15-32, 94-100), otherwise from env FIRECRAWL_API_KEY (:101-108). SAFE_MODE (= CLOUD_SERVICE) strips `actions` and crawl `webhook` (:136-137, 205-220, 442-452). Transport is stdio by default, or stateless httpStream for CLOUD_SERVICE / SSE_LOCAL / HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER (:566-594), with a /health endpoint (:110-116). Other modules: src/types/fastmcp.d.ts (ambient types for firecrawl-fastmcp); docker/nginx.conf + docker/entrypoint.sh (Dockerfile.service image: nginx on :8080 in front of node on :3000, rewriting /{apiKey}/... path keys into the X-Firecrawl-API-Key header); src/legacy/index.md (the pre-FastMCP implementation kept as a Markdown file, not compiled). The server itself implements no retries, credit tracking, output-size caps, retrieval timestamps or content hashing, and sets no default for maxAge or onlyMainContent; those are left to the SDK/API.

No provenance flag, id-token permission, attestation, checksum, signature or SBOM step exists in any workflow (grep of .github found none). Docker: image.yml pushes ghcr.io/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server:latest from Dockerfile.service on every push to main (image.yml:6-37); image-staging.yml pushes ghcr.io/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server-alpha:latest from the staging and fastmcp branches (image-staging.yml:6-40). risks: Documentation does not match the v3.2.1 code: the README documents firecrawl_batch_scrape, firecrawl_check_batch_status, 'deep research', FIRECRAWL_RETRY_*/FIRECRAWL_CREDIT_* settings and arguments timeout, maxDepth, systemPrompt, lang/country (README.md:20, 193-203, 363, 375-432, 486-487, 530, 583), but src/index.ts registers six tools (src/index.ts:234, 273, 314, 402, 470, 497), reads none of those env vars and defines none of those fields (src/index.ts:171-232, 375-385, 429-456, 536-543). It does not document the CLOUD_SERVICE, HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER, PORT or HOST settings the code reads (src/index.ts:56-58, 566-577). Tool descriptions still tell the model to 'use batch_scrape' (src/index.ts:241-242, 279, 408-409), and the search example passes sources as strings (src/index.ts:346-348) while the schema requires {type} objects (src/index.ts:381-383). VERSIONING.md describes /:apiKey/v2 endpoints that exist only as an nginx rewrite in the Dockerfile.service image (docker/nginx.conf:10-46; VERSIONING.md:16-24) and a test-endpoints.js script that is missing (VERSIONING.md:93-101; package.json:18).

Scope: the fetch and interaction capabilities named in the needs are reachable only as MCP tools backed by a remote Firecrawl service - no CLI and no library export (package.json:6-11; no process.argv in src/index.ts). A Firecrawl account and API key are required for the default cloud API (README.md:82, 182-190), or a separately run self-hosted Firecrawl that is not part of this repo. Every URL, option and typed text goes through @mendable/firecrawl-js (src/index.ts:268, 309, 394, 462, 562), including the `text` of write actions (src/index.ts:211), which would carry any credentials typed in a scripted sign-in. Tool descriptions also instruct the model to default to these tools ('you should always default to using this tool', src/index.ts:238, 317).

Page interaction is limited and undocumented: it exists only as the `actions` array (wait, screenshot, scroll, scrape, click, write, press, executeJavascript, generatePDF; fields selector, milliseconds, text, key, direction, script, fullPage) (src/index.ts:164-166, 205-220); the README never mentions actions, screenshots or PDF (grep). It is removed when CLOUD_SERVICE=true (src/index.ts:137, 205), has no tab, navigation, cookie/session or file-transfer action types, and each tool call is a separate client.scrape request (src/index.ts:268), so this repo keeps no browser state between calls. Its limits and timeouts are defined in the SDK/API, not in this checkout. In default stdio mode the model can also set executeJavascript scripts (src/index.ts:215), skipTlsVerification (src/index.ts:222) and crawl webhooks with custom headers (src/index.ts:442-452).

No automated tests: zero test files, and jest/ts-jest/eslint/prettier are undeclared (package.json:55-57; package-lock.json); jest.setup.ts mocks removed SDK methods (jest.setup.ts:52-66); `npm run test:endpoints` targets a missing file (package.json:18); CI only runs npm ci and npm run build (.github/workflows/ci.yml:22-26).

Runtime and lockfile inconsistencies: package.json engines.node >=18 (package.json:36-38) while @mendable/firecrawl-js 4.3.4 requires >=22 (package-lock.json:58-60) and yargs 18 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=23 (package-lock.json:1904-1906); CI and publish use Node 20.x (.github/workflows/ci.yml:19; publish.yml:18) while the Dockerfiles use Node 22. package-lock.json says version 3.1.9 (package-lock.json:3) against package.json 3.2.1, and the two lockfiles resolve different @mendable/firecrawl-js versions (4.3.4 vs 4.3.5).

Release hygiene: npm publish runs from CI with a long-lived NPM_TOKEN and no provenance, attestation, checksum, signature or SBOM step (.github/workflows/publish.yml:27-30; grep of .github); GHCR images are tagged only `latest` and rebuilt on every push to main (image.yml:6-10, 35); workflows use actions/checkout@main and old v1/v2 action majors with no `permissions:` blocks (image.yml:17-30; image-staging.yml:20-33); neither Dockerfile sets USER; typescript is a runtime dependency (package.json:33); the main server dependency firecrawl-fastmcp is a separately published fork whose source is not in this repo (package.json:32).

Inbound auth in HTTP modes: with SSE_LOCAL or HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER, authenticate checks no inbound credential and returns the server's own FIRECRAWL_API_KEY (src/index.ts:101-108); the bind host is localhost by default but overridable with HOST (src/index.ts:567-570), CLOUD_SERVICE binds 0.0.0.0 (src/index.ts:568-569), and /health is unauthenticated (src/index.ts:110-116). The service image's nginx accepts API keys embedded in the URL path and rewrites them into X-Firecrawl-API-Key (docker/nginx.conf:10-46); the file sets no access_log directive (docker/nginx.conf:1-122).

Maintenance and licensing signals in the tree: CHANGELOG.md stops at 1.7.0 (2025-03-18) while the package is 3.2.1 (CHANGELOG.md:3; package.json:3); the server advertises name 'firecrawl-fastmcp' and version '3.0.0' (src/index.ts:89-90); the pre-FastMCP implementation is kept as src/legacy/index.md; LICENSE names 'vrknetha' as copyright holder while package.json author is 'firecrawl' (LICENSE:3; package.json:50); one transitive dependency (uri-templates 0.2.0) declares its license as a URL rather than an SPDX id (package-lock.json:1833).
